verdict.rationale: Cursor documents scoped API-key mechanisms usable for agents: service accounts are non-human credentials that can be created, rotated, and revoked for automation without tying to personal accounts (cursor-supp-service-accounts), API keys carry named scopes (e.g., 'Required scope: admin:*') and per-endpoint rate limits (cursor-supp-apis-overview), and CLI agents can be constrained via least-privilege permission tokens for shell/file access (cursor-supp-cli-permissions). This covers issuing restricted, non-personal credentials and limiting agent action scope, but the granularity of API-key scopes shown is coarse (single admin scope example) and there's no documented fine-grained scope picker or independent verification. Missing for 10: evidence of granular/custom scope selection when generating keys, and independent/hands-on confirmation of least-privilege enforcement.
